observation.visible_scene: A fixed night view of a snow-covered outdoor shopping promenade decorated for the holiday season: a Starbucks storefront on the left, a hanging 'CHEEZED' sign and light-wrapped garland on the right, snow-laden tables and a closed umbrella in the foreground, and an illuminated Christmas tree with glowing cone-shaped structures in the background. Snow falls continuously through the frame. Two pedestrians in dark winter coats occupy the left-center walkway, with a few smaller figures near the lit structures in the distance.
visible_changes: The two foreground pedestrians in dark coats steadily recede away from the camera down the path: their heads rise and their bodies shrink in the frame, and they drift toward the image center (left person from ~x160 to ~x240, right person from ~x270 to ~x315) as perspective compresses their spacing.
Snowflakes appear as moving white specks/streaks descending across the sky and foreground throughout the clip.
A background figure in a tan/brown jacket shifts slightly rightward over time (~x335 to ~x360).
The glow around the central tree and the cone structures changes hue/intensity between frames (whiter early, more purple/blue later), suggesting animated holiday lighting.
Foreground snow-covered tables, umbrella, railings, garlands, and signage remain in fixed positions relative to the frame edges.
outside_clip_unknowns: The starting point and destination of the two walking pedestrians, and what lies beyond the receding path, are not shown.
The cause of the lighting color shifts on the tree/structures is not visible.
Whether snow accumulation changes on surfaces is not determinable within this short excerpt.
uncertain_details: The camera appears static (background architecture and signs do not translate), but no parallax is available to fully rule out tiny drift.
The apparent hue change of the background lights could be animation or compression/exposure variation; not certain.
Exact clothing details and identities of the pedestrians are obscured by distance and low light.
